why: Nothing in production changes (a scan, a JSON baseline, a test case and docs), and most counters are named exactly, but the test is self-referential: whatever the counters return is written as the baseline by --first, so a counter that counts the wrong thing passes forever. Two places need a reader: the dispatcherJobs counter reads the runJobs object in the cart-reminders route, which step 1.10 moves to src/server/dispatcher-jobs.ts, and the twins list is typed by hand from step 0.42's verdict files, which is a judgement of what is kept on purpose.
harm_if_wrong: A budget that holds the wrong figure (zero dispatcher jobs, a guessed link count) or lists a fold as a tolerated twin, so later growth passes unseen; no store or shopper is affected.
make_it_cheaper: Point dispatcherJobs at Object.keys(DISPATCHER_JOBS).length from src/server/dispatcher-jobs.ts (step 1.10) plus the tracked() calls, and write the twins entries verbatim in the brief, so commit 1 needs no judgement.
brief_problems: dispatcherJobs is counted from lines after runJobs("dispatcher" in src/app/api/cron/cart-reminders/route.ts, but step 1.10 (an earlier step) moves the job object to src/server/dispatcher-jobs.ts; stop_if 3 names only step 3.3's registry, so the cheap model will find no lines or stop.
